components.goal: Control the bilinear coupling term in the source energy estimate.
components.key_estimate: Source Eqs.(13)–(15): telescoping cross terms and Young's inequality yield positive coefficients 1-sqrt(tau sigma)||K|| and 1-tau sigma ||K||^2.
components.name: primal extrapolation
components.operation: After the dual and primal proximal updates form xbar^{n+1}=2x^{n+1}-x^n.

limitations.statement: The extracted gap rate is ergodic and restricted to bounded test sets; it is not an unrestricted global-gap or last-iterate rate.
No guarantee for inexact proximal maps, theta other than 1, or boundary tau sigma ||K||^2=1 is extracted.

performance_links.scope_note: Theorem 1(b,c) under this exact Model and update rule; bounded-test restricted gap applies to averages of updated iterates.

variants.cost: Inspection of Eq.(7): one K product, one K* product, one prox_{sigma F*}, and one prox_{tau G} per iteration. Charge each operation separately; arithmetic, extrapolation and running averages require vector operations and storage. Internal proximal solution cost, operator-norm information and gap evaluation are additional; no gradient-only Oracle Complexity claim is made.
variants.implementation_details_ref: §3 Algorithm 1 Eq.(7), PDF p.6 / printed p.4; §2 proximal definition, PDF p.5.
variants.name: Algorithm 1 with theta=1 and fixed positive steps
variants.output: For the restricted-gap rate return x_N=(sum_{n=1}^N x^n)/N and y_N=(sum_{n=1}^N y^n)/N. Raw iterates x^n,y^n converge to a saddle-point under the stated finite-dimensional assumptions, without a raw-iterate gap rate in this extraction.
public_inputs: K and K*, G and F* through their proximal maps
Positive tau,sigma satisfying tau sigma ||K||^2<1; a valid operator-norm upper bound suffices for conservative tuning.
Initial x0 in X, y0 in Y; iteration horizon N>=1.
variants.query_and_update: For n>=0, first compute v=y^n+sigma K xbar^n and y^{n+1}=prox_{sigma F*}(v). Then compute w=x^n-tau K* y^{n+1} and x^{n+1}=prox_{tau G}(w). Finally set xbar^{n+1}=2x^{n+1}-x^n.
variants.requirements: X,Y finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces; K continuous linear; G,F* proper convex lower-semicontinuous and nonnegative as formulated in §2; F* is the conjugate of convex lower-semicontinuous F; a saddle-point exists. Exact prox_{sigma F*} and prox_{tau G}, K products and adjoint K* products are available. prox_{a H}(v)=argmin_u {H(u)+||u-v||^2/(2a)}.
variants.state_and_initialization: Store x0,y0 and set xbar0=x0. Maintain current primal/dual iterates and the previous primal value; optional running sums start at zero and include updated iterates 1..N.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Keep tau,sigma fixed and theta=1, with tau sigma ||K||^2<1. Run a prescribed positive integer N. Theorem 1 gives a horizon bound, not a computable stopping certificate requiring an unknown saddle-point. Boundary equality and inexact prox are not covered here.
